utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone after the break of more than a week. I am happy to see that everyone is there again. Mr. Stamp, the Chamber expected the Prosecution to come up one of these days, or perhaps even today, with a new schedule of the witnesses, but I don't know whether it is at this very moment that you would like to inform the Chamber or that it will be at a later stage today or tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It should be certainly tomorrow. We are in discussions, as we are just about coming to the end of the shelling crime base part of evidence, and a new structure should be with the Court certainly this week, but I would expect by tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's try to make it tomorrow, if possible. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, is there anything else you want to bring to the attention of the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There are some documents which the Prosecution proposed to tender personally under Rule 92 bis. But perhaps with your leave, we could do so at a more convenient time later in the day, and at this moment, proceed with the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if the witness is there, I think we could start with the witness and whenever there is an opportunity today, then you perhaps bring it to our attention what the Prosecution intends to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. The Defence would like to take this opportunity while we are waiting for the witness to advise the Chamber that the health situation of General Galic has significantly worsened. With your permission, we talked to him on the telephone this morning and if with the Court's indulgence, General Galic would like to say something about his health, whether now or at the end of the day. It is up to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since I was informed that we -- that the witness is waiting already --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I suggest the following order: That General Galic will briefly address the problem he is facing at this moment, and if it needs more time to discuss it or to see what has to be done at this very moment, then we perhaps do it at a later stage, so that we are briefly informed now and we can also then decide whether it is so urgent that we deal with it in more detail at this moment or that we do that on a later moment today. General Galic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am aware that discussing health problems in public is not the most pleasant thing to do, so if there is any specific reason why you would like to raise the issue in other circumstances, in closed session, for example, please indicate so, so we can take the appropriate measures.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Mr. President. There is no need for closed session. I am quite comfortable to discuss it in open session because I believe that the issue concerning my health is publicly known; we have already mentioned it a couple of times. I will be very brief. It is my spine, Your Honour, that causes me problem. The situation has worsened. I am under therapy. I take medicine three times a day, three or four different medicines which are painkillers. However, it disturbs me to a certain extent for the purpose of following the trial. Likewise, I have problems with walking. The guards have been very considerate, but I still have to crouch a couple of times before reach the courtroom. I should like to be examined once again. A CT of my spine has already been done and I believe that the results have been provided to the Chamber. I don't know the details, though. So I am sure that you are familiar with the general situation of my health. The problem, Your Honour, is a discus hernia, which has caused three different injuries. One of them is a major one and causes considerable pain. I have been provided with a special chair here, as you can see it, and this chair has somehow, to a certain extent, alleviated the problem. Likewise, I also have a plastic chair during the break, so I am able to relax a little during the break. However, in the detention unit, I asked for a special chair on several occasions because I spend a lot of time, reading, writing or watching TV. However, nothing has been done in this respect so far and I do hope that Mr. McFadden, the chief of the detention unit, will do his best. I know that he is currently working on this problem. If this situation should continue, I do not think that I will be able to follow the trial under, let me say, normal circumstances. The pain very often suddenly appears in the area of my hip and my spine and moves up towards my head. And once I have this headache, I have difficulty following the trial. So, Your Honours I should like to ask you once again for my health to be analyzed by a professional physician and, if possible, I should like to have a team of doctors to visit me from Belgrade. These doctors are employees of the military hospital in Belgrade who followed me in the past and who monitored my health in the past, and they have all the necessary documentation, and I should like to be examined by them and have a conversation with one of these physicians in the detention unit. The doctor here in the detention unit, when I told him this, said that this is a good idea. And that perhaps in the meantime I should do some exercises, physical exercises. However, the problem is that I cannot really walk. If I were able to walk normally, things would be much easier. I am regular with my morning exercises, and so far, they have helped me to endure and to follow the trial. So my suggestion is a very simple one, Your Honour: I should like to be examined once again. I should like to have an opinion whether a surgery is necessary or not. But once again, if the situation is allowed to continue in this way, I do not think that in the future I will be able to follow the trial. Thank you very much for your attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you -- if you prefer to be seated, that is no problem, as far as the Chamber is concerned, General Galic. Are you under any treatment, apart from getting medicines, by physiotherapy or something like that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, Your Honours, it is very difficult to organise physiotherapy to continue with the trial at the current pace. I know what kind of exercises I have to do and I do them every morning, but I was not treated by a physiotherapist. I hope that you have understood me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think what the Chamber has to do is enquire further into the questions you raised, and it is a new examination, also especially aiming at getting an answer to the question whether surgery would be a solution for your problems, and preferably not only by the doctors in the detention facility but also assisted by the doctors who have treated you before. That is one issue. The second issue is the chair in the detention unit. I do understand that the chairs here have improved, but not yet in the detention unit. We will enquire to that further, and when it needs more discussion in this courtroom, we will come back to it. For this very moment, are you at this moment able to continue with the trial? You told us several times that if it would not change, that in the near future, you saw major problems in attending the trial. But for this very moment, I mean today, and, well, let's say the week to come, do you feel able to follow the -- to attend the trial and to understand and concentrate enough to make it a trial as it should be?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I am an old soldier, you know, and I am accustomed to enduring thing as lot. But if you want my personal opinion, I think I will be fine for this week. You know how it is, the situation is not the same all the time. Sometimes I have more pain, sometimes less. Well, I wanted to be as brief as possible. For the time being, I think I will be able to follow the proceedings, with minor difficulties which, as far as I am concerned, I don't think affect to a great extent my ability to follow the proceedings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will make sure that, with high priority, we will pay attention to the issues, the health issues, you have just raised and we will come back to it. Well, then if there is no other issue to be discussed at this very moment, Mr. Stamp, who will be the next witness to be called by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Fata Spahic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Spahic, I presume. From your reaction, I take it that you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I invite you to speak clearly into the microphone so that we all can hear you and that the translators also can translate to us what you just said. Ms. Spahic, before giving testimony in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth -- that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. And the text of this declaration will be handed out to you now by the usher. And may I invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I am afraid we didn't hear the first part of the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just invite you to make the whole declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am afraid I cannot see the text. I don't have my glasses with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, may I ask you to repeat the words that I will read out to you. Would you please repeat me. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The whole truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The whole truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Spahic. Please be seated. Ms. Spahic, you have been called as a witness by the Prosecution and that means that you will first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution. Then, later you will be examined by counsel for the Defence and if the Judges have any questions, you will hear from us as well. Mr. Stamp, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Spahic.

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Spahic, I think it is easier -- Mr. Stamp is putting questions to you; he is sitting to your right. If you are a bit nervous, there is no need to be nervous. Mr. Stamp will put questions to you, and perhaps if you look at him, he is standing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: To your right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't have to look at the screen all the time, Mrs. Spahic. That is Mr. Stamp who is -- he is over there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am afraid I cannot read --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Spahic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- what's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't have to read anything on the screen. Just look to your right. Mr. Stamp is standing there and he will put questions to you. Yes? Listen carefully and try to answer his questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your name is Fata Spahic?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, Fata Spahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Which city do you live in, Mrs. Spahic?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How long have you lived in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: For 35 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you have a family there?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How many family members are there?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Four.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And did you live in Sarajevo during the period 1992 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In what part of Sarajevo did you live at that time?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: In Svrakino.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where is Svrakino? Is that a part of a larger district in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: It belongs to the Novi Grad municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And in that period in time, in particular, 1994, with whom did you live? Did you live with anybody in particular?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: With my husband and my two sons.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you remember the 4th of February, 1994? Did something happen?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That day, did you leave from where you lived and go anywhere in particular?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: To Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you tell us briefly why you travelled to Dobrinja that day?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: To get some flour for my children.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Tell us, if you can, about the circumstances surrounding the supply of food and flour at that time, why it is you had to travel to Dobrinja to get flour.

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: They had more humanitarian aid than we did. That is why we went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And how --

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: To swap flour for cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I take it from your answer that you would go there to trade flour for cigarettes, generally. That day, the 4th of February, 1994, was that your intention?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And can you remember about what time you set off to go to Dobrinja to get this flour?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Around 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And did you set off to Dobrinja alone or did you have company? Did you have other persons travelling with you?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No. I was not alone. There was some friends with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you remember the names of your friends?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Fatima Sito and Azra Spahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think I heard you call another name which I don't see recorded. Could you repeat -- could you tell me how many friends then travelled with you?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you have Fatima Sito and Azra Spahic. Can you recall the third name of the friend that travelled with you?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I am afraid we didn't understand the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the last name, Mrs. Spahic, because the interpreters couldn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Pribinja Muskija.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And do you know what was the purpose of them going to Dobrinja? Was it the same purpose as yours, to trade for flour?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, how did you travel to Dobrinja? By what means did you travel there?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: On foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This was a time of conflict, and I take it that it might have been a little bit dangerous?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Tell us how you managed to get there by foot if you managed by any particular strategy?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We tried to hide from the bullets. The bullets were whizzing all about us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And how were you dressed?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: As a civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, can you remember the clothes that you had on?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: I had camouflage pullover.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the other ladies, how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: In civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What was the weather like that day, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: The weather was nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How about the visibility?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: There was some fog.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: At what time was there this fog?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: At about 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Can you tell us about what time did you arrive in Dobrinja, approximately.

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: About 10.00, 10.30, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And did you go to any particular place in Dobrinja to do the trading for flour?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No. We walked to see once when they come out of town so that we can see what we can trade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, where in Dobrinja did you go to, to do the trading?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: It was Oslodobilaca Sarajevo Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you go on the street itself or did you go somewhere in the vicinity of that street?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No. We just went between the buildings to hide from the bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, where did the trading for flour, where was it expected to take place?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: In Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And what I am really asking you, was it on Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street itself or was it somewhere close or in the vicinity of Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: There was a field and we were on there, a play area, that is where we were, on that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The witness has already answered -- it's a little objection because the witness has already answered that this was in the Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street. But considering that the witness already answered, I would in fact withdraw this objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said there was a field with a play area there. Where was this field with the play area in respect to Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: They have those garages there between buildings, so there is some kind of parking lot or a play area; that is where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, about how many persons gathered in this play area?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: There were about 20 or so of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And can you recall if the persons there were men, women, children? What was the composition of the crowd in terms of age and gender?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: It was all women there and there were some children. There were little girls that also came for the flour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And how were these women and little girls dressed, can you remember?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: All in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What did you carry there to trade that day?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Cigarettes, flour, that is some dried spinach leaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And did you put your cigarette and dried spinach leaves anywhere in that play area?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: There were three benches and we put it all around on these benches.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, while you were there that morning, did anything happen?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: A shell fell opposite to where we were when we arrived. And we fled.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We will take this bit by bit. You said, "a shell fell." Let us take it from the start. While you were in that play area, did you hear anything?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: There was a whistle.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you please describe exactly what you heard after this whistle.

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Just heard cries for help, screaming in those buildings near us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you heard this whistle, could you say if the whistle was going in any particular direction?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Well, the shell landed on a building, fell on a building.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you heard this whistling, did you do anything?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We fled from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where did you run to?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: To an entrance where humanitarian aid was distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you said the shell exploded on a building. Did you hear anything when this shell exploded?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We heard screams for help, cries.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And can you say where the shell exploded, on which building the shell exploded?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: To the right of where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you say "to the right," tell us in terms of the garage. Where did the shell explode in respect to --

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: In a flat. It exploded in flats. That is where the shell landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And this flat, where is this flat? Can you remember the street this flat is on?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: It is Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street. It all happened in this street.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said you ran to a passage from which you heard screams. How long did you remain in that passage?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: About 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And did you do anything after those 15 minutes elapsed?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We went back to get our things.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What things are you speaking about that you went back to get?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We had those spinach leaves and all the other things that was -- that remained on the benches.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you said, "we," meaning yourself and other persons. Were these other persons the other women who had --

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, when you returned to get your things, tell us now --

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We all went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am sorry, I did not -- oh, "We all went back." When you all went back to the play area, what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We heard this sound, and as we bent down, the shell landed near us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What sound did you hear? You said you heard this sound and "the shell landed near us." Can you tell us what you saw and what you heard when the shell landed?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We heard the noises, and when we heard the noises, I turned back, and then there was fog and I was all covered in fog and I couldn't see anything. And then I saw these two women who -- who were down and I tried to help them, and I couldn't help them. And there were injuries, head, leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said you heard noises. Could you describe what type of noises you heard when the shell exploded?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We heard the whistle, and we heard and then it fell. As soon as we heard it, it landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did it land in front of you, to your side, or behind you?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Behind us. Behind our back.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And after it landed, you said you were all covered in fog. What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what the shell made. There was this tar and dust that came from the shell so we realised that the land -- that the shell had landed. We couldn't find our bearings.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am going to ask you Mrs. Spahic, just to speak about what you and you alone saw and heard. Okay? Don't tell us what you believe other people there would have seen and heard. Just adhere to what you saw and what you heard. After the shell fell, did you see -- did you see people around you and in what condition were these people?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: They were --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object, Mr. President. I am objecting because there were two questions that follow on each other, so if the answer was "I didn't see anything," so I don't know why the following question would be in which conditions they were. So if we look at the question, is that it is indicating to the witness that the witness should have answered "yes" or "no." So that is the reason for the objection. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am trying to be as careful as I can with the witness, having regard to everything which is pretty obvious. However, I do recall the witness saying that there were two ladies who were being down --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two women being down, yes. I don't think that since the witness did already testify that she saw two women down, that it would not be appropriate to ask whether she saw any people around and in what condition. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp. You may answer that question. The question was whether you saw any people around you at that very moment after the shell landed.

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did see them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And in what condition they were?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Some were crawling on the floor towards the buildings and there were two people who were killed, and the others were crawling away towards the buildings. They couldn't -- they were also injured people.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The two ladies that you referred to earlier, did you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Fatima Sito and Muskija and Azra.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Fatima Sito, and who is the other person.

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Muskija Pribinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In what condition was Fatima?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: She was all black from the tar dust and her leg and her head were injured, were smashed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And Muskija Pribinja, what condition was she?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: She was injured and she calling for help. I couldn't help. And they took her out and then the ambulance came.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said you couldn't help Muskija. Did you go anywhere after this?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: They took us all to the surgery in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who took you?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Some people from this surgery.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think you mentioned ambulance. Did they take you in an ambulance?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: They had a car. I don't know who called the ambulance, but they had a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In which vehicle -- did they take you to the surgery in a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: It was a small ambulance vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Tell us about yourself now. Were you injured?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was, I was injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: To what part of your body? Just tell us.

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Right arm and my leg, the lower leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said you had on a flack jacket. Where did you get this jacket from?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: From my son.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you notice anything about the flack jacket after you had been taken to the surgery?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: I saw there were lots of shrapnel in it. I could not be recognised, there were so many pieces of shrapnel in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you indicate what would likely have happened to you if you did not have that flack jacket on?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Well, I think I would have been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is just a presumption, assumption. I don't know how we can ask this kind of question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: While you were being taken to the surgery, did you hear anything in particular?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We heard another shell falling right there where we were, where we were injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know what was -- what, if anything, was taking place on Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street that day?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: There was -- there were other people injured. I don't know, myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The people, the other people on Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street, do you know why they were there that day?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Well, there was humanitarian aid that was being distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: About how long after you returned to the playground area did the third -- did the second shell explode that day?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: About 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to intervene for the French transcript because there is a problem of interpretation. We are not -- they are not mentioning the second shell, and I think we should do that, be very careful about the reading of the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In English, it was quite clear. When you were talking about 15 minutes, is that the time between the first shell landed and the second shell landed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, about 15 minutes was the time between the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And following on from that, you said you returned to the playground area to pick up your things. How much --

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How much --

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How much time elapsed between the time when you started to pick up your things and the shell fell behind you?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: 15 minutes. We went back from there to pick up our things.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I understand that. And how soon, if I may put it another way? When you started to pick up your things and a shell landed behind you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We started to pick up our things and as soon as we started doing that, I remember that the shell fell immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall participating in a video production last year with an investigator of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you indicated to the investigator while being videoed certain places, to the best of your knowledge and recollection?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we did. We showed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: After the incident of the 4th of February 1994, when was the next time that you returned to that playground?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: I didn't. It is when I went -- I don't know which month that was. It was in spring. I don't know exactly when.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, you said you didn't -- perhaps if I could clarify this. You were there on the 4th of February, 1994, and you were there sometime last year showing our investigator certain places, to the best of your knowledge and recollection. Did you return to that place before --

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am not sure if I follow your answer. You were answering before I finished the question. Did you return to that place before, anytime before you showed our investigator the various places?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No, we never returned. No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I take it from your answer that between the 5th of February, 1994, and the date when you did -- when you were videoed there, you never returned to that place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No. Certainly, we did not go back. We did not return.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, with your leave, I respectfully ask to play for the witness to identify videotape P3281.E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Leave is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: For the record, it is P3281.E. P3281.E as in "echo."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just for the record, please, the document that I have in front of me is 281E, P281.E. I don't -- I don't know whether we have the same document. The one that I have is 3281.E, which is not what we see on the transcript. 3281.E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I take it that you have studied the video before this -- before today, and you just check whether it is the same or not and then I take it that the -- that the number of the video, as pronounced in words by Mr. Stamp, will be the final number.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with pleasure, but, however, the number that we have just been given is not the one that has been pronounced by Mr. Stamp, and that was the reason of my intervention. I have 3281.E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If Mr. Stamp is telling us that it is 328, then it's a different number

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He said it is 3281.E, so that's exactly the same number as you mentioned. If there is any confusion after we have seen the video, please come back to it, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I do not see anything on my screen at this very moment. We could now play the video. "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: The other personnel remain the same. Mrs. Spahic, I am now going to give you some instructions. Could you please show me by standing at the spot where, to the best of your recollection, you took shelter after you heard the first shell explode on the 4th of February, 1994. I will repeat my question: Where you took shelter after you heard the first shell explode. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: I see you are indicating down the sidewalk. Could you please indicate once again for the camera. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Thank you."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you please stop there and rewind just very slowly. Stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mrs. Spahic, do you see a sidewalk in the middle of this frame?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: At the end of this sidewalk, in the direction of where you are pointing, is that the passageway that you said you ran to?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Please proceed. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we please proceed in the normal speed. "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Could you please show me by standing on the spot where you were, to the best of your recollection, on the 4th of February, 1994, when the second shell exploded? "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Can you please stand on the spot. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: May I just confirm that this is the spot where you were standing when the second shell exploded on the 4th of February, 1994? "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: I am going to mark this spot with yellow paint and an X with the number 2 on it."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you stop here, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mrs. Spahic, beside the investigator, there are two columns there. Do you see them? Look on the video.

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Having regard to those columns, can you say where the bench with your goods was set up?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness be asked to repeat the answer, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The question is: Can you tell us where the bench that you had laid your goods to trade was set up?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Near the passageway, near the playground where the garage is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this: You said that that is a place that you are standing at the time when the shell exploded behind you?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We were standing next to the bench, and the shell landed behind us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And is that place where you are standing now where the investigator just marked with the spray paint, the place where you were standing when the shell exploded?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Where the yellow marking is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mrs. Spahic, and that place where the yellow marking is, is the place that you were standing when the shell exploded; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we proceed with the tape in normal speed. "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Could you please show me by standing at the spot where, to the best of your recollection, the second shell exploded on the 4th of February, 1994? "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Thank you very much for your assistance. We will now proceed to the third location."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. You may stop here. Thanks. Your Honour, Mr. President, may I just indicate that this is perhaps, we could say, a presentation with three episodes. As I indicated the last time, the witness Ljusa was involved in the first, this witness is involved in the second, and a third will be played when another witness is here to identify that part. So that is a presentation. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that also explains that the other personnel remains the same as we started with. Yes, I now do better understand. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You, Mrs. Spahic, you answered the questions asked and gave the indication that you did on this video to the best of your knowledge and recollection?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said that you did not return to this place after the 4th of February until you went there last year with our investigator. Can you tell us whether or not this explosion and the incident in which you were injured had any psychological effects on you?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Well, there have been changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What changes? Could you please describe them.

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: First of all, I have often pain in my arm, especially when I work for a longer period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And lastly, that day, the 4th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am very sorry, Mr. President, but the French record is as follows: "I suffer; I am in pain." It is not the same thing as "I have often pain in my arm." One has to be very precise in cases like these. Thank you for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mrs. Spahic, may I ask you, when you said you have often pain, did you say that you often have pain in your arm or were you referring generally to having pain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Always in my arm, but when the weather changes, the pain is more severe in my arm. But my leg hurts all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How about mental and psychological effects? Are there any which have resulted from this incident that we speak of?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes. I am very often fearful. Whenever I hear a sound, I immediately think of a shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And finally, did you see any soldiers on Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street that morning?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, two soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And at the place you were injured, at the playground, did --

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Before, that's where we saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We will get to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The French booth that I am following have just told us that they were not able to hear the witness's answer. Perhaps we should have it repeated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it about the presence of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was the last response which was given by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you told us, Mrs. Spahic, that you saw two soldiers, Mr. Stamp asked you whether that was on the place where you were injured at this playground and then you answered the question --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not there, but before. Not at that spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let's again take it step by step. You said you saw two soldiers. Where did you see two soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We saw the two soldiers on the way to Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you say, "on the way to Dobrinja," was that before you reached into Dobrinja that you saw these two soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: When we got into Dobrinja, that is when we saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: About how far, if you can estimate the distance, from the place where --

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Fifty metres, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Fifty metres from where?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: From the place where we were injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where were these soldiers; could you tell us precisely?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: I don't know the names of the streets there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers that morning on Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street where the people were gathered for humanitarian aid?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No, but before.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The soldiers that you saw before, about how long before did you see them? How long before you arrived at Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street did you see them?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Maybe five minutes before.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And after you saw them, you walked for five minutes before you arrived at Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: At the playground where you had set up your goods for trading, did you see any soldiers or weapons there?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you saw these two soldiers, were you in Dobrinja or was it before you reached into Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: In Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Nothing further. That is the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The French booth didn't hear the last answer. Mrs. Spahic, was the last answer you gave that you were in Dobrinja when you saw these two soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hope this will clarify the question from the French booth. Is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness? It will be you, Mrs. Pilipovic, as I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Spahic, you will now be examined by counsel for the Defence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mrs. Spahic.

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us that on the 24th of February 1995 -- 1994 - I'm sorry - you gave a statement to the officials at the Public Security station in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you also confirm that on the 26th of June, 2001, you spoke to the investigators of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you signed these two statements?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And that you confirmed by placing your signature on the statement that the contents of the statements accurately reflected what you had stated?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Spahic, you told us that you lived in the Novi Grad municipality?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In which street, please?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: In Partizanska Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this street is located in Pavle Goranin neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is your neighbourhood situated below the Mojmilo hill?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Spahic, you spoke about 1994, and February the 4th, that is the day when you went to Dobrinja. During 1992, 1993 and 1994, were you employed, please?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were you employed before the outbreak of the conflict in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you work?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: In a school.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Where is the school located?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Before the war, it was located in the area of Dobrosevici.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What part of Sarajevo is that in relation to your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Alija.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that there were four members in your family, that you have a husband and two sons?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In 1992, 1993, and 1994, were your husband and your sons employed?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were they members of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you were wearing your son's flack jacket?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As a member of the BH army, did your son have a uniform?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What about your other son and your husband, did they have a uniform, too?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When did they join the BH army?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: I don't know what year it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I may refresh your memory, was it in 1992 or 1993?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Which military unit were they members of, your husband and your sons?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: My son belonged to the corps, he was a member of the corps, and then the fourth one -- I am sorry, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Throughout the time that they were members of the BH army, did they have a uniform?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did they have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Not much.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us at what lines they were deployed as members of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: In Vares.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How often did they come home?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: My husband would be away for two months, but the sons came home more often.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When did your sons come home? You said that they came more often. How did they go home?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: On foot.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how far their positions were from where you lived?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Some 200 metres away up there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You say "200 or 300 metres away." Can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Well, 300 metres away approximately. I didn't measure the distance.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said 200 to 300 metres away. Are you referring to the positions located in the vicinity of your house, where you lived?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, where we lived.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You say that your sons were deployed at the positions which were 200 or 300 metres away from the place where you lived. Do you know where they were actually quartered as soldiers while they were there?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: They were accommodated in the houses up there, and in the cellars.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You say, "in the houses and the cellars." Did anyone live in those houses or were they empty?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: They were empty.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who used to live in those house since now they were empty?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: I don't know. These people had left, had fled.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the neighbourhood of Pavle Goranin, and you said that the positions were 200 to 300 metres from there. Was there any fighting going on in that part of town?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How often would that fighting take place?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Every 10 or 15 days. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did your sons tell you that the BH army was deployed at the Mojmilo hill? Did you know that from them?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On that day when you set out for Dobrinja on the 4th of February, who was with you?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Fatima and Muskija.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to Fatima Sito?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What about Azra, who you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Azra Spahic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And Muskija Pribinja, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Before the 4th of February 1994, how often had you gone to Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: I had never gone to Dobrinja before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So was that the first time that you went to Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is time for your break, as far as I can tell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I don't even have to ask you, Ms. Pilipovic. Thank you for your assistance. Mrs. Spahic, we will have a break of half an hour and then you will be further examined by Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 11.01 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Spahic, you told us before the break in answering my question that, on the 4th of February, 1994, it was the first time that you went to Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Spahic, you confirmed that on the 26th of June, 2001, you gave a statement to the investigators of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Spahic, from your statement that you gave on the 26th of June, 2001 - this is page 02081011, paragraph 3 of the statement - I would like to show you, read to you a part of your statement, and I would like to ask you what is correct.

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: I will tell you the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: "On that day, that day was not the first day I was going to Dobrinja. Before I went with some women there."

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: I went to Dobrinja for the first time on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Spahic, you said on the 26th of June, 2001, that you went to Dobrinja before with some other women. Could you please tell us what is true? Is it true what you are saying today or what you told the investigator?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: What I told the investigator, I went --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter's comment: The answer isn't very clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Your answer isn't very clear.

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: That is the first day that I went to Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you are confirming that it was that day that you went first time to Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So what you are saying is that what you told the investigators that you went to Dobrinja before is not correct?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: I did not go before.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you answer why you told the investigators that you went to Dobrinja before for food?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Spahic, when you gave the statement to the investigators of the OTP, did you speak to them in your own language?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you finished the interview, what you said, was it read back to you?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you sign that what you said was true?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did sign.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So once again, could you explain to us what is the truth?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: The truth is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, you made your point. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Spahic, you told us today that on that day, the 4th of February, you went to Dobrinja with Muskija Pribinja, Azra Spahic and Fatima Sito?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Spahic, in your statement that you gave to the investigators

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So she was already there when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So on that day, she did not go together with you from your house to Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us why did you say in your statement that you went with her?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that I said that in my statement that she went with us. We met her there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you are now confirming that what I have just told you, read from your statement, that you went with her, that is not correct?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No, she did not go with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On that day when you went to Dobrinja, could you tell us which road did you take to get to Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We went from Mojmilo. We went through connecting corridors between trenches.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Spahic, you went -- you said you went through trenches, corridor trenches?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: That's right, up to a point.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us about these trenches, these corridors? Was this also used by the army?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, after you went through these trenches, how did you get to Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We went through the buildings, in between the buildings.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: These trenches that you mentioned through which you went, you said that the army used them. Could you tell us which army?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know which army it was. We went through the trenches, but I don't know which army was using them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On the way to Dobrinja, while you were going through the trenches, did you see soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The houses that you mentioned that this is where the positions were and where your sons were on the line, could you tell us how long did your sons spend on those positions, on those lines on the houses?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: They spent there a lot of the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say, "a lot," do you mean to say all the time, day and night?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So they spent all that time on the positions?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you confirm that they slept there and ate there?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: That is right, yes, up there in those houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the HQ was of their unit?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Of the younger one?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you said, "the younger," what do you mean? In relation to Mojmilo hill, where was it?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Down there, Mladjani. It is a settlement, it is a locality down from Mojmilo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: It is from Dobrinja or from the other side?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: It is facing Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Asked by my learned colleague, you said that it was 50 metres from where you were on this plateau and where the shell landed, you said that it was 50 metres from there that you met two soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: It was a little bit before that plateau that we saw these two soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were these BH army soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose so. We didn't ask them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Spahic, did you speak to those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that in your statement you said there were three Bosnian soldiers --

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: There were two.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that you spoke to them, could you tell us what you spoke about?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: They asked us where we were going.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What did you tell us -- what did you tell them?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We told them that we had to go and get some flour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did they warn you that you should not be going to Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: They said we should better be hungry than go there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you that it was better to stay hungry than to go there?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Well, when they know there is going to be firing, they told us we better get back.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When I tell you that in your statement on page 2, 012 document, that the soldiers told you that Dobrinja was a very dangerous place because of intensive shelling and firing which was happening there all the time, can you confirm that this is what they said?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did they try and talk you out of going to Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: They tried to talk us out of it, but we had to get some food for our children.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, on the way from your street towards Dobrinja, did you hear some shooting?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, we heard shooting. There was whistling, bullets were whistling past us, shells landing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that on that day in that area where you were moving in, was there combat?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: I don't know where combat was. There were shells. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that you heard?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We heard shooting, firing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the part of town where you lived, in the locality of Pavle Goranin, was there a school?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us in relation to your settlement, your locality, how far is Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: About 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether in that part of town there were schools?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: There were no schools anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say, "there were no schools anywhere," are you trying to say that the schools were not operating at the time?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: They were not working at the time, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether there were soldiers stationed in those schools in that part of town?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know anything about that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the part of town as you were going towards Dobrinja, apart from the trenches, were there also barricades in that part of town towards Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: I don't know. We did not go in that area. We didn't dare to.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I think that you answered in the examination-in-chief that it was sunny weather but that there was some fog?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Well, there was some sun and, yes, there was a little bit of fog.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement that you gave the investigator, you said it was a fine and sunny day, with good visibility.

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: It was that, too, and it was -- there was some fog as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you -- did it take you to go from the place you lived to the place where you went to barter for flour?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: One hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you and your friends that you went to Dobrinja on that day, did you receive information in any way that there would be distribution of humanitarian aid on that day in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that before, there was distribution of humanitarian aid in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us who told you that you would be able to barter for flour in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Well, some neighbours went before and they told us that it was possible to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you that there would be distribution of humanitarian aid?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived at Dobrinja in that part of plateau that we saw on the video, could you tell us how many people were in that plateau, in that area?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: There were about a dozen. Ten or so.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, when you heard the first shell falling, in relation to that plateau, where did it fall?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: It fell near the buildings.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that the first shell landed behind the building?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: It landed -- it fell on the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to see that?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We only heard people crying out for help.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you didn't see the shell?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We could see where it had fallen in the flat, but we only heard the cry for help.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You confirm to us today that after 15 -- that 15 minutes later, you were nearby when the second shell landed?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us from your friends who were with you?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Muskija, Azra and Fatima, and there were others. There was also Zumreta, and there were others whose names I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us about the injuries that your friend sustained?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Azra had a thigh injury and Zumreta had an injury in her right leg. Fatima was hit in the head and the leg.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you were wounded as well.

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what injuries did you sustain?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: I was lower -- right lower leg and right arm.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you were in Dobrinja hospital?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive a medical certificate that you received treatment?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you give your medical documentation to the OTP investigators?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No, we did not. Nobody asked for it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Considering that we are talking about the time of armed conflict in Sarajevo, could you tell us, in the part of town where you lived, what was the water supply situation?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Very bad.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say, "bad," could you elaborate on that?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We did not have water so we went to the Novi Grad municipality at night.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you had no water?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We didn't have water. We had to go and fetch it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: For how long did you have no water during the day or during the week?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We had no water. It would happen perhaps for a month or two in that settlement. We did not have water.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you confirm that the tank for supplying water in that part of town was in Mojmilo?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: It was in Vrace.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know that the tank that was supplying water was in Mojmilo?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know. They told us it was from Vrace. I don't know where it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say you were told that it was from Vrace, who told you?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Well, when it was war until they would let it -- until they would switch it on in Vrace, we wouldn't have water.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us how did you get electricity?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We did not, we had no electricity.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that you had no electricity, could you tell us during which period you had no electricity?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We had no electricity for a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before my friend proceeds to the next question, I am wondering if the record here is correct at line 44 -- at page 44, line 8. I think I heard the answer being, "It was Vrace." Question: Could you confirm that the tank for supplying water in that part of town was in Mojmilo?" And I think I heard the answer being, "It was in Vrace."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which might be confusing because the word "Vares" has been used today before and, as I take it, referring to a different area. Could you please clarify this with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Spahic, in response to a question that I put to you regarding the shortage of water, you said that they -- you didn't have water because they didn't switch it on at Vrace. Are you telling us that Vrace is the location in which they said that there was no water?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is what they said. For as long as they didn't switch it on at Vrace, we didn't have water.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about a water tank at Vrace?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: That's what they said, but I don't know, I am not sure, for our neighbourhood, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
