utterances.text: You told us that your sons were deployed at some 300 to 400 metres away from where you lived and that they were accommodated in houses there. Can you tell us how long this line was along which the houses that they were using were situated?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. All I know is that they were accommodated in the basements of those houses. But we didn't move around in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us about the area where the houses were and where the BH army was along those lines, which were 300 to 400 metres away from your house. Do you know whether the VRS forces were deployed in the vicinity?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were. They were at Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When your sons came home, you said it was always for two months?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: One month or two months, but they wouldn't stay very long. They just came to change their clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When they came home, were they armed?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In your neighbourhood, were there any troops there?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So it is your testimony that the troops were some 300 to 400 metres away from where you lived?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, or maybe even further than that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On that day when you went to Dobrinja on the 4th of February, 1994, you said that your friends had been wounded on that day. Do you know how many people were killed or wounded on that day?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: 28 of us were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if anyone got killed?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: I know that these two women got killed and a young man -- two young men. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that two women and two young men were killed. Do you know whether these two young men were there at the very spot where the incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were. They were boys. I saw them, but I don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this concludes the cross-examination of the witness, but with your permission, we should like to tender witness statements in evidence, but we do not have copies at this point. We will make copies and tender it later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I notice that you have read a few lines of the witness statement. Could you please indicate what would be the specific reason why you would like to tender the whole statement, because we usually proceed in a way that --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to tender only two pages of the statement and two paragraphs from the statement which the witness confirmed, for the purposes of credibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stamp, is there any --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I would know the purpose of tendering two pages. The statement itself is really two pages. Perhaps the portion that counsel feels important could just be read, and I think they were read. I don't think it is necessary to tender the entire statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, as a matter of fact, that was my question as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You pointed at...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is fine, Your Honour. It is okay. Thank you. We have no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just a couple matters of clarification, if it pleases you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said that you know that two young women were killed. Do you know the names of these two young women?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Fatima and Muskija.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I take it that those were the two women that accompanied you?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said there were two young men, boys, you later indicated?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where did you see them?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We saw them not very far from us, maybe three metres to the left. They were killed, but I don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Spahic, I have a few questions for you. The first is that you told us that your husband was at Vares and that --

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- he was away for two months. Could you tell us where Vares is? Is that close to your house or is that far away?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Well, it is far away. It is far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it outside the city of Sarajevo or is it --

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, outside the city of Sarajevo. Behind the mountain, the Treskavica mountain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then you have told us that you used trenches while going to Dobrinja, trenches that were used by the military as well. You also told us that you did not see any military in these trenches. Could you please explain to us exactly what you mean by "trenches," the trenches you used while going to Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Because we wanted to hide from the shells. It was a dangerous area because of the proximity of Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but could you tell us exactly what you understand by "trenches."

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Those trenches had been dug up so that the military could use them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so they are not built-up trenches, but they are dug-up trenches?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, dug out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They are not used by military at the moment when you used them to go to Dobrinja; is that true?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We didn't see the soldiers at the time in those trenches, but we had seen them before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you know of any other trenches closer to the confrontation line with the opposite armed forces?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, my next question is: You told us that you were warned by the soldiers you spoke to about the firing, the shelling in Dobrinja, that was why Dobrinja was a dangerous place to go, they told you. Could you tell us in the place where you lived that was in Pavle Goranin, as far as I understand, was there frequent shelling as well or was there never shelling or -- ?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Half of the houses are gone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I do understand that apart from Dobrinja, a dangerous place, in your place there was shelling at -- with what frequency? Could you tell us? Once a year? Once a month? Once a day?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Every other day or once in three days, one of the houses would be destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My last question to you is: You told us that you had no water in the place where you lived, apart from when someone turned on the water from, as you told us, from Vrace. That's what they told you. Could you tell us, Vrace, was that controlled by which party to the conflict?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I think that the area of Vrace was shelled from Lukavica. I believe that was the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You tell us that it was shelled from the area of Lukavica, but do you know who was in control of Vrace? Was it held by the BH army or the ABiH army or was it held by the Republika Srpska or --

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: The army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, Mrs. Spahic. You have not only answered --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is just one, if I may, area which I respectfully ask to ask about it, and it is an area which arose in respect of an area which you asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it is in relation to a question I asked, I will grant leave to put an additional question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said that you had --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I may just have a moment to get the verbatim response.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said, "We didn't see any soldiers at the time in those trenches but you had seen them before." Can you understand from that that the soldiers which you refer to as having seen that day, you saw them before you reached to the trenches?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: When we came out of the trenches, we saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And could you say exactly where those trenches are?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Below Mojmilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you saw these soldiers when you came out of the trenches below Mojmilo, is that what we are to understand?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That is all, may it please you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I also ask you for one clarification, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you said you had seen soldiers before in the trenches, do you mean to say on that same day or on another day?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: We saw these soldiers when we came out of the trenches. Whether they had been in the trenches, we don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. Ms. Pilipovic, you have an additional question?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to clarify, Your Honour, to follow up on your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Spahic, you told us that the trenches were located below Mojmilo.

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And that you came across these soldiers there. The area of Mojmilo, this particular area of Mojmilo, is it facing -- does it face Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Lukavica. I am sorry, I don't understand you. It is facing Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So how far is it from Dobrinja? Did the Lukavica road go in between? Was that the division line?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Lukavica road divided these two areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was it necessary for you to cross the street when going from Lukavica and one would immediately find oneself in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't go there. We didn't dare go along the Lukavica road because of the shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As for these soldiers who stopped you, where exactly did you cross the street? How did you reach Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: It was coming from the direction of Mojmilo that we crossed over to Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you said you crossed over to Dobrinja from Mojmilo, can you be more precise, please? Which particular street did you take?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: Well, we walked in between buildings there. I don't know about the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In order to reach Dobrinja, was it necessary for you to cross the Lukavica road?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't cross that road.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What street did you have to cross coming from the direction of Mojmilo in order to reach Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: FATA SPAHIC
utterances.text: I don't know the names of these streets.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mrs. Spahic, you have answered all our questions, questions from the Bench, questions from the Defence, questions from the Prosecution. It is important for us to hear the testimony of those who have been present at the relevant times and the relevant places. So, therefore, I would like to thank you very much for coming your long way from Sarajevo and for giving testimony in this court. I know it is a long way back as well. So I wish you a safe trip home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please escort Mrs. Spahic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, am I right in understanding that we only have the video played P3281.E, and that is admitted in evidence as far as it was not yet admitted in evidence because it has been used before, as far as I understand, part of it, and the second part which is relevant for this testimony is -- I hear that it is a new exhibit and it will be used again a later stage of the proceedings. So it is admitted into evidence. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The next witness, if we can proceed to that, is Muhamed Kapetanovic. Can he be brought into the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we want to ask the usher, we have to wait first until he is back.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In the interim, I understand that the procedure in respect to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher -- unless you need much time, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, no, I don't need much time. There was an issue I mentioned this morning in respect to the 92 bis (C) statements of the deceased witness. I understand the procedure here is that the statements be formally tendered to the Court, in court, on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but are these -- is this one of the deceased witnesses we --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Two deceased witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's Mr. Sasi [phoen] and Mr. Sopi. You know that there is an appeal pending on the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would rather discuss first with my colleagues on how to proceed. As far as I understand, we have certified an appeal and, as far as I understand, the appeal, meanwhile, has been lodged. So I don't know what is the best way of dealing with it. But I will discuss this with my colleagues and I will let you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please bring in the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kapetanovic, I presume. Mr. Kapetanovic, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before giving testimony in this court, Mr. Kapetanovic, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text of this solemn declaration will be handed out to you now by the usher, and may I invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated, Mr. Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, you will first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Stamp, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you please state your name.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Muhamed Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And what is your date of birth, Mr. Kapetanovic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: 24th March, 1984.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In 1994, where were you living?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: In Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where in Sarajevo was this?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: In the Alipasino Polje neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you remember the street name?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Cetinska, house number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is that presently the name of that street?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What is the name of it now?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Goeteova Street, Goethe Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And who did you live with at that time?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: With my father, my mother and my sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us about the circumstance in which you lived in that area? Firstly, did you notice anything about shelling in respect of that area?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was this area shelled at all?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: About how frequently while you were there?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Two to three times a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, the area, the building that you lived at, is it -- what type of building is it?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: It was a high-rise residential building with 16 floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And what was in front of that building, can you say?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: There was a parking area in front of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you said that area was sometimes shelled. Could you tell us a little bit more precisely, what part of the area was shelled?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Some of the shells hit the buildings and some landed in the vicinity around the buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, can you recall the 22nd of January, 1994?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you go anywhere that day?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I went out to play with my friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you remember where you went to play?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. We went to play outside the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is there any particular place outside the building that you went to play?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Near the parking area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you remember the names of your friends?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Their names were Daniel Juranic, Admir Ahmethodzic, Elvir Ahmethodzic, and the fourth one, I cannot remember his name. Actually, his name was Kenan. I don't remember his family name.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am going to ask you to give us those names again, but do it little bit more slowly, because I don't see the names on my record. Just tell us the names again slowly of the friends that you went to play with.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Daniel Juranic, Admir Ahmethodzic, Ahmethodzic Elvir, and the name of the fourth was Kenan. I don't remember his family name. Elmir and Admir Ahmethodzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. How did you play? What did you play outside the parking lot?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: We were sledding in the snow.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And what was the weather like that day?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: It was a sunny day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And can you tell us what happened as you were there sledding?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: We were sledding and then we suddenly heard that shells were falling. We knew that it was nearby because of the loud noise, the explosion, and then we got very scared and started to run away. But before we managed to get to the entrance of the building, a shell landed behind us. Daniel Juranic was killed. I was injured in my head, leg and arm, and then the Admir and Elvir were also injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, you said -- I have it here that you said that shells were falling and then you heard a loud noise? How many shells, shell or shells, did you hear before you started to run?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was one or two, for sure. One or two shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How far from your apartment building were you playing when you heard these shells explode?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: About 100 metres, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, did all of you run to your apartment building or did some of you run?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: We all started to run towards the building, towards our building, except for Kenan, who went into the next door building.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said another shell landed behind you. Can you say about where that shell landed?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Approximately about 10 metres, perhaps less, behind Daniel, who was the last one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When it landed, where were you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I was about 10 metres from the entrance hall of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you said you were injured. Can you tell us about your injuries? What was the nature of your injury?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: The worst was the wound on my leg. The doctors fought for a long time to save my leg. That is why I had to go to Italy to be treated, while the other injuries that I had on my arm and face were not quite so serious.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. After you were injured that day, were you taken anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was in Italy to be treated, but before that, I was administered first aid in Dobrinja. And after that, I went to the Kosevo hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And how long did you remain in the Kosevo hospital?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: About 40 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you said you went to Italy for treatment. How long did you stay in Italy?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Two years.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Briefly, what type of treatment did you get for your leg?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, because in Sarajevo there were no means for my treatment, I had to go there and I was given treatment to save -- to be able to save my leg. I had seven operations in total.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: At the area that you were playing that day, were there any soldiers there or any military activity going on in that area in front of your building?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No, there was nobody. It was a quiet day. There was no shelling on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, do you know of any facility in your neighbourhood that is associated with the military?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In -- there was an annex building and it was a detachment. It was a -- local troops were stationed there called Kulin Ban.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where was this in relation to the front of your apartment where you were injured?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: This staff was located behind my building.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How far from your building was it located?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: 150 metres, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the place that it was located at?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question? I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the place or the street that it was located at?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: The street was called Rade Koncara Square. That's what it used to be called. The name has changed since.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What is the name of it now?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I think it is Nezavisnosti Trg, Independence Square.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said local troops were stationed there. About how many -- why do you say local troops were stationed there?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: There was an APC in front of their staff. People came there in uniforms, and from there, they most probably went to the front lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. You said an APC. What do you mean? Could you describe what you mean by an APC?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: They made these APCs, these armoured vehicles, manually. They put metal sheeting on top of the glass windows in order to protect them. These were armoured vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: They put metal sheetings on top of the glass windows. Were these armed regular vehicles before with glass windows?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When had you seen this vehicle at Rade Koncara square?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Last time, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I ask it differently? Did you see the vehicle at Rade Koncara square once or more than once?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: More than once.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Approximately how frequently did you see it there?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: About two to three times a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And when was the last time you saw it?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Four or five days. Before I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, did you obtain a medical record from the Kosevo hospital?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you gave these records to an investigator of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, with your leave, I ask to tender to the witness Exhibit P2174, and to the Court, that exhibit as well as P2174.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is -- have you had a look at that document?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is that a copy of your medical record from Kosevo hospital?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said you heard one --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may take that document away.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I thought the last -- I saw on my screen Prosecution counsel confer so I was just waiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said you heard one, maybe two, shells explode before you started running. Could you say where you heard the explosions coming from?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Now, the place where the shell which injured you landed was somewhere behind you, you said. You were about 10 metres from your building and the shell landed about 10 metres behind you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry. There is a problem of interpretation. I think it is the French booth. I am sorry, Mr. Stamp. But we have to be very certain about the indications that Mr. Stamp gave. What has been interpreted in the French booth is not what Mr. Stamp asked in relation to the number of metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stamp, I didn't follow the French translation, so I still do not know what the difference was. But if you would please repeat your question and I will change to the French channel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I will rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How far were you away from your building when the shell exploded?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Ten metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you said earlier that the shell exploded about ten metres behind Daniel, who was the last one. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am sorry. We have problems in the interpretation. What Mr. Stamp said is that the shell exploded ten metres behind Daniel, but again, that is not what is coming from the French booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we have to be very precise with regards to this description.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will just read slowly what the question was, and would you please also listen carefully, Mr. Kapetanovic. The question was: "How far were you away from your building when the shell exploded?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ten metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then you said earlier that, "The shell exploded about ten metres behind Daniel, who was the last one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Everything is clarified, I think. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So from that, could you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: From that description, can you recall approximately how far from the entrance of your building the shell exploded?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: About 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And from the front of your building to the back, what is that distance in metres? Can you estimate it? From the front of the building to the exit at the back of the building, what is that distance?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: About 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And what is immediately behind your building? Could you please tell the Court.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this Kulin Ban staff was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: To get from the back exit of your building to Rade Koncara Square, where the staff was, how would you travel, or would you travel through anywhere in particular?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We -- there was a window that we broke in the cellar, so we would go through this window and then you would get to the Kulin Ban. So it would be through the cellar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, may I just interfere for one moment. Your answer to the question: "How far it was from the front of the building to the exit at the back of the building," what was your answer exactly? Was it 15 metres or 50 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 50. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you exit your building at the back, immediately as you step out the cellar or the back exit, where would you step into?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: That would be the ground behind the building. It would be the opposite side of where I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Tell us about that ground behind the building. What exactly is that ground behind the building?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Before it used to be a school yard. It was a basketball area of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How wide was this ground -- from the back exit of your building to the building across the ground, how far was that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: 15 metres, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And on the other side of that ground, what did you have there?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: There was the building where Kulin Ban was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you said the ground was used as a playground. Was it paved or not?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Some parts have asphalt and the other parts have grass.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Your building, you said, was a 17-storey building. Were all the buildings on your street that high?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Except where Kulin Ban was stationed, it was lower. It had four or five storeys.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in 19 -- I beg your pardon, the year 2001, did you participate in a video recording with an OTP investigator?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And did you show that investigator the area that you were injured, to the best of your knowledge and recollection?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your leave, and the leave of the Court, may I ask to be played for the witness, P3281.F?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, leave is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could the Exhibit P3281.F be played. "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Will you please indicate by pointing the general area where, to the best of your recollection, you and your friends were playing on the 22nd of January 1994. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Will you please show me by walking to and standing on the spot where, to the best of your recollection, a shell landed which wounded you on the 22nd of January 1994. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Mr. Kapetanovic, will you now please show me by walking to and standing on the spot where, to the best of your recollection, you were located when you were wounded on the 22nd of January, 1994. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: I will now mark this spot with yellow paint and a figure X with a number 2 beside it. Finally, will you please indicate by pointing the general direction to the best of your recollection from which you ran after you heard the first shell explode on the 22nd of January, 1994. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: My question was quite clear. I want to know, please, from where you started and which -- first of all, point to the direction from which you started, to the best of your recollection. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: And please indicate, to the best of your recollection, in which direction were you running. "THE WITNESS: [Indicates] "THE INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Thank you."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just, Witness, ask you about your injury. You said you spent two years in Italy, where you had to have several operations. Do you still have any physical effects as a result of your injury?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What is the nature of these physical effects?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: The leg I was injured at is about two to two and-a-half centimetres shorter. I have to use orthopaedic aids and I cannot do any sports, any contact sports.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And how about psychological and mentally. This incident occurred when you were quite young. Do you have any enduring psychological effects as a result of this injury?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think I have any.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very good. Now, with the leave of the Court, I would like to show you, Witness, a photograph and this, Mr. President is P3678.C.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp, do you think we could finish this in one or two minutes? If not, we would perhaps rather first have the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Perhaps we can have the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, we will take a pause for 20 minutes and we will then resume your examination. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, you were about to show a photograph --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, I am going to ask you to have a look at this Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. photograph. Can you see clearly, Mr. Kapetanovic?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you make out some writings on the building which you see in the photograph now?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Where do you make out these writings? Could you describe it, where you see these writing?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: In the middle of the photograph, the name of the video club. Is that what you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am wondering, Mr. President, if I may be allowed to vacate counsel's role to have a look at his screen because it might well be that the quality on his screen is better than the quality on my screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was one of the issues, I was just informed by the Registrar that it could be changed. I must say, I have a perfect picture on my screen, and to my left and right-hand side, it is still good. I see Madam Registrar has a bad --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: If you use computer evidence, it is much better there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it comes directly from your computer. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, what about your screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For once, our screen is excellent. The witness has read out from the screen a moment ago. We can ask him once again. He has read the word "discotheque" and we can ask him for clarification.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not "discotheque," but videotheque, a video club.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, since all our screens are clear, we can all verify that it is videotheque. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp, if at least the quality of the image is good enough to proceed. If there is anyone who has made your complaints -- I don't hear anyone, so please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The building where you see that sign, which building is that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: It is the building at number 4 Cetinska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you turn the video clockwise? Yes, to the right. Could you stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This part of the video which you just saw, are these the apartment buildings that you and your friends were running to?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you continue in the same direction. And stop here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you look further down the street in front of you, which is in the middle of this part of the photograph, do you know where Cetinska Street stops?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: In the background of the photograph, to the left part of the photograph, you see a yellow newsstand. This is the end of Cetinska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, I have some difficulties in following the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That newsstand is just adjacent to the sidewalk, to the paved part of the sidewalk? Is that so?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't know if the Court has observed a structure adjacent to the paved part of the sidewalk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you -- I see a yellow structure just under a tree. But I don't know whether that is what the witness was -- perhaps you could guide him with the cursor, to let him follow the cursor and indicate where exactly he pointed at. Could you please give, Mr. Kapetanovic, directions to the one who is moving the cursor where you find this newsstand, and say by going to the left or up or down so that we can better follow your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you see the cursor? It is in the middle of the street.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Should it -- to find this newsstand, is it to the left or the right? Could you just direct us to find it?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: To the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And could you tell us if we have found it, please.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Stop, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think the witness is indicating a yellow structure adjacent to the paved part of the sidewalk which seems to be under a tree, indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I would say at the fourth small grassy area, to the left of that. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, going passed the end of Cetinska Street and further down that road, which street would you go on to?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Klara Zetkin Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, Klara Zetkin Street is still known by that name today, is it, or has the name changed?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: The name has changed. It is now Bosanska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you continue turning to the right, please. Continue. Stop here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is this a parking lot in front of your building that we have just --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We are going to turn slowly, and could you tell us where it is that you were playing when we reach to it? Can you do that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: To the right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you say where, about where? You could describe it by some structure that is on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Next to the green structure, to the right side of the photograph, next to this low-rise building.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you turn a little bit to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Are you referring to --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you stop, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Are you referring to the green structure with a brown base, which is --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Please turn to the beginning. I am sorry. Please go in the original direction. Thank you. I think we have gone right around.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Kapetanovic. Is this photograph you have just seen a photograph of the area in front of your apartment building where you were injured?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We may take it off the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you a couple of questions about this playing area to the back of your building. About how big was it? What was the size of this playing area?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: It was quite big, but then again, not too big.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. What was the distance across the playing area from the back of your building?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I am sorry, I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: From the back of your building, if you were to cross the entire playing area to reach the buildings at the opposite end of the playing area, what distance would that be?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: 100 to 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the buildings across the playing area from the back of your building would be the buildings at Rade Koncara Square?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That, Mr. President, Your Honours, is the evidence in chief for the Prosecution. May it please you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague will conduct the cross-examination of the witness. I just wanted to know where this 360-degrees photograph was taken from. I think the witness was asked at two points to specify the location and it didn't come across very clear. So I should like my learned friend from the Prosecution to specify exactly from which vantage point the photograph was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It was taken from the location where the witness indicated the shell fell, the shell which injured him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can see, the photograph could not have been from the other location. Ms. Pilipovic, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, you will now be examined by counsel for the defence. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You testified today about a shelling incident in which you were wounded and in which Daniel Juranic, your friend, was killed, the incident in which a number of your friends were also wounded. On that day when this incident occurred, what was the weather like; can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: It was a clear day.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any other children and people moving around the area at that time?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any other children sledding at that place?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: They were in front of which entrance, which house number were they in front of?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me think. They were in this other street that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Klara Zetkin?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What is the name of your street now, the one that used to be Cetinska Street?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: It is now called Goeteova Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you were sledding in Cetinska Street and the other children were sledding in Klara Zetkin Street. How far away from you were they?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: About 300 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us today that you were sledding, and you showed to us a green house on the photograph where it was. You were there at that spot. Where exactly did the shell fall?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the first one?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: The first one fell in Klara Zetkin Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know outside which house number it was?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether there were any children there as well?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, five children were killed in Klara Zetkin Street, and a number of them were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: From the place where you were, where you were sledding and you said ran from in the direction of the street where you lived, Cetinska number 4 --

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No, number 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Number two, I apologise. Did you see the shell land from that spot?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I couldn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You only heard it fall?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that there were people around the area. Do you know, in light of the wounds that you sustained, if there were any other persons, apart from those that you have mentioned, who were wounded from the shell that hit the area outside your building?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, not many were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What was the time distance between the first -- between these two impacts?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you cannot tell us how much time elapsed between the two?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness be asked to repeat the question? We didn't hear it. It Is either ten minutes or ten seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether on that day other shells hit that area of the town where you lived?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your previous answer was not well understood by the interpreters. Were you talking about ten seconds or ten minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ten seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is what I understood. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, is it correct that you gave a statement to OTP investigators on the 12th of February, 2000?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Before that, did you have any other interviews to -- concerning this incident? I am referring to relevant officials.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us today that the Kulin Ban detachment had its headquarters behind your building.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You used the word "detachment." Do you know how many members this unit had?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that this was a detachment in the sense that it was a military formation or is it something that you heard from others?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: This is what I heard from others.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you used to see these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you describe for us how they were dressed?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning, they didn't have any weapons. Later on, I believe that they received uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of uniforms? Can you describe them for us, please.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just ask for a clarification. Your question was, Ms. Pilipovic, "Can you describe for us how they were dressed?" And then the answer was, "In the beginning they didn't have any weapons. Later on, I believe they received uniforms." Is that what you answered, because it changes from dress to weaponry and it seems a bit illogical to me, but it might be --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that my question was how they were dressed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And was then your answer that, in the beginning, that they had -- didn't have any weapons or -- ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that, at the beginning of the war, they didn't have weapons or uniforms. Later on, they got them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that they wore camouflage uniforms, but that at the beginning of the war they didn't have enough weapons. Are you telling us that, later, they were better armed, they had more weapons?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: They had some kind of rifles for the purposes of defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you used to see these soldiers in this area and did you see them with weapons?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, because it was from there that they went to the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We will get to the front lines later on. Let us now focus on the building where these soldiers were accommodated. Was it a residential building?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was. They were accommodated in the basement of this building.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You are referring to the basement of a building located at Rade Koncara Square?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What house number was this, can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke today about Rade Koncara Square and a school yard there?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that there was a school in the area?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: The school was located in the so-called C settlement, maybe five minutes away from where I lived.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How far was the school from the building where this military formation was located?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Also four or five minutes away.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You went to school at the time?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was a student.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you attend classes at the time?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Actually, yes, but not in that particular school. The lessons were held in the basement of our building.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What was the name of the school?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I forgot what the name used to be. It is now called Mesa Selimovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you went to school but that you didn't actually go to the school building. Do you know whether the building of the school was used by anyone at the time?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether on this square where this headquarters were and the school building, whether there were any other locations such as police? Did the police have their premises there?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if there was a Civil Defence headquarters there?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was humanitarian aid distributed in the area? Was there a room which was used for that purpose that you went to, to get humanitarian aid?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: We went to collect humanitarian aid in another building, at house number 3 in Cetinska Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that Cetinska 3 is not part of Rade Koncara Square?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No, Cetinska Street does enclose Rade Koncara Square from one side and Klara Zetkin encloses it from the other side.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke about the members of the Kulin Ban detachment. Do you know to which army the Kulin Ban formation belonged?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that they went to the front lines, do you know -- in view of your age, then, do you know where the front lines were?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement that you gave to the investigators, you said that you went to the front line with your father?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what part of town is that, where the front lines were?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: It is a hill above the C phase. It is above the street of Klara Zetkin Street, and on the other side of the hill was the front line and we went to the other side to get the wood because we didn't have any wood.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "hill," can you tell us the name?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Mojmilo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The front lines on Mojmilo hill, could you tell us which army was there?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I mean, I don't get your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you find out then when you went with your father to the front lines, which army held these front lines? Was it the BH army or was it the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't go all the way to the front lines. We would go beneath the hill while the front lines were on the other side on top of the hill. But I think they were held half and half. Half was held by the BH army and half was held by the VRS army.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the period of 1992, 1993, 1994, in that area, the area of your settlement, did you hear that there was combat between these two armies?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I heard, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether -- or could you tell us how frequent these combats were?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In your settlement, I am speaking specifically about Alipasino Polje, Rade Koncara Square, could you tell us what was the electricity supply like and water supply like?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: We had electricity occasionally, almost none, but for water we had to go and fetch it to another settlement which is beneath the C phase settlement. This is where we had to go and fetch water.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that there was electricity occasionally, can you tell us what that means? What does it mean, "occasionally"?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: What I mean is, perhaps two days a week, we would have electricity.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know in the part of your settlement in Sarajevo, were there electricity cuts?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I was a child then. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that you went to fetch water in A phase settlement area, was that at that time the part called Trg Zavnobih? Is that where you went to get the water?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether that area I went to get water was called Trg Zavnobih.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is that now the International Friendship Square, Trg Prijateljstvo [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you describe for us the A phase, because we are talking about A, B, and C phase, what part of the settlement is that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, "A" would be the first part of the settlement going along the tram track. That would be the first part, that would be the "A" phase. And then the difference would be that "B" and "C" would be along this square.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to the "A" phase, how far is the television building away from that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: In that part is nearby, that would be opposite the television building, and where we got the water, we fetch the water, was perhaps some 400, 500 metres from the television building.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We are talking about the television building. Are we talking about the Oslobodjenje building where television was, or some other building?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the BH television?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Well it is in the A section, A phase. It is in the municipality building.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the Oslobodjenje building?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No. You mean the newspaper, Oslobodjenje?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Oslobodjenje is a completely different part of town in Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How far is your building from the TV building?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Some 10, 15 minutes walk.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you told us that you went to the vicinity of the front lines with your father, in that part of the settlement and the direction that you were going towards the front lines, were there trenches?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice whether in that part of the area near Mojmilo hill, were there trenches?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean now?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: No, then.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from the soldiers that you identified as members of the Kulin Ban unit in the area where you lived, in that settlement, were there other soldiers that you saw?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean other units? You mean members of other units?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, no, because Kulin Ban was some kind of local unit, I mean of that area, of that "A" section.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether in Rade Koncara Square there was a restaurant called "Stela"?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And on that square, was there a coffee bar called Borsalino?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, in the beginning of the conflict, in the part of the settlement where you lived at that time, were there so-called paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, may I remind you that in the beginning of the conflict, the witness was eight years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, but he spoke about the front lines, which is the reason why I asked him some other questions as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, when you spoke about your friends who were injured, do you know about their injuries, I mean about Elvir and Admir?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Admir's leg was amputated. He had a high amputation of the left leg. And Admir also had an injury of the left leg -- of the lower leg.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Today, you clarified for us where you were at the moment that the shell fell and your friend, Daniel, who was killed. Could you tell us, at that moment, where were Elvir and Admir?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: They were running in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you described your position and that of your friends, could you tell us, is it possible to see where the shell fell?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is there a trace from that shell that landed?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you describe, in relation to the location where you were, how far is the crater, so to speak, of that shell?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Ten metres from me, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to your friends?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. We were very near each other. There wasn't more than one, two metres between us.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you told us that you heard the first shell, could you tell us when you found out that other girls and boys were injured or died?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: A few days later, when I came around to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were you together in the same hospital?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean Admir and Elvir?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And other children.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, we weren't, but Admir and Elvir were in the military hospital, but they were only there for two days and then they were transferred urgently to Italy. Admir had some 12 operations or something like that, and then his leg was amputated.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In that area where you were sledding, was this your usual play area? Did you play there before?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how frequently?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: That depends or depended, rather, on shelling. If there was shelling, we would be playing in basements. But if days were quiet, then we would go out.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the area where you lived, could you tell us how frequent were the shellings?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Two or three times a week. I think I already said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Which facilities were usually shelled in that area when you say that it happened two or three times a week?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Some shells fell on residential buildings and some would end up in the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: At that time when you said that there was shelling and that shells were falling, did you hear shooting, firing, from other weapons?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that there was shelling in certain parts of the area where you lived, where you were, did you hear firing from other weapons as well?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that there was shelling and that it happened two or three times a week, could you tell us that you saw the shellings?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if anyone was killed?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean names?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In your part of town.

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I recall, I had a friend who was also injured about a month before us. He was injured on the square, on the Rade Koncara Square. He was wounded there. I don't know his -- I don't remember his name. I have forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would just like to consult my co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I see that you are standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. This is not a question, but I believe that would not come out either in the French or in the English transcript, and I am talking about page 78, line 12, where the witness was talking about - and I think this could be important - this is to do with combat, when he was referring, Mr. President, to this military unit which was located near the incident place, he used the expression which is not what we find. I believe this is in line 22. I apologise. Yes. Instead of what we are seeing that they were going towards the front lines, I believe that the witness used "Borba" [phoen] which means combat, which even indicates a more active term. I don't know whether you could perhaps ask the witness what he meant because it doesn't appear in French or in English transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I could ask you, Mr. Kapetanovic, you were asked by the -- you used to see soldiers in the area and whether you saw any weapons with them, and your answer then was, "Yes, I did because it was from there that they went to ... " To what exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That they went to defend. They went to defend the city of Sarajevo. They went to the front lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think this clarifies the issue. Mr. Stamp, is there any need for re-examining the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Earlier, when I was asking you questions, you indicated that one, perhaps two, shells fell before you started to run, and you were unclear where they fell. And just now in response to my learned friend, you said the first shell fell outside Klara Zetkin Street. Could you tell us precisely what sequence -- in what sequence did this shelling occur? Did the first shell fall outside Klara Zetkin Street or did you hear an explosion before that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: We just heard the explosion. We didn't see where it had fallen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So when you said that the first shell fell outside Klara Zetkin Street, that is something you heard afterwards; is that so?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And it is possible that two shells might have fallen before you started to run; is that so?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In the area where you live in Alipasino Polje, which phase was that?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: That was "C" phase, "C" section.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was there any combat in that area, in "C" section, that you know of?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No, not in the "C" section itself, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was there any confrontation line in the "C" section, that you know of?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: I am sorry, could you repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was there any confrontation line between two armies in "C" phase of Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And finally, could you just please, if you can, spell the surname of Elvir and Admir. Can you?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Ahmethodzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. The spelling was not clear when you first answered. Were they related?

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they were brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp. Mr. Kapetanovic, I have one question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were asked whether in the period of 1992, 1993, and 1994, in the area of your settlement, whether you heard there was any combat between the two armies. I think you said, "As far as I heard, yes." That could mean two different things: As far as you heard from other people, or as far as you heard with your own ears. As far as the combat activity was concerned, could you tell us what you meant by "As far as I heard."

utterances.speaker: MUHAMED KAPETANOVIC
utterances.text: It is what the adults told us, people who came, these soldiers who came from the front lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much for your answer. Mr. Kapetanovic, you came a long way from Sarajevo to this courtroom. We are all aware that you were still rather young when the events happened you testified about today. You have answered all the questions of both parties and of the Bench, and you will certainly be aware that it is of great importance for this Tribunal and for this Chamber to hear the answers of those who were present at these times and these places. Therefore, I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please escort Mr. Kapetanovic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you please guide us through the documents or rather videos and CD-Roms, but we will start with the documents as far as I am aware of.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3281F, video; Exhibit P3678C, 360-degree Quicktime movie; Exhibit P2174, medical documentation in B/C/S; Exhibit P2174.1, English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, since there are no other objections as the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. standing objection against the 360-degree photograph, they are all admitted into evidence. I do see that the experience from some 10, 11 days ago was encouraging the parties. We will adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00 in the same courtroom.
